newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NOL's planned takeover of APL positive - analysts.
newsitem.headline: NOL's planned takeover of APL positive - analysts.

text.p: Neptune Orient Lines' (NOL) planned takeover of U.S. container carrier APL Ltd should give NOL instant access to the huge U.S. market and bring substantial savings, investment analysts said on Tuesday.

Investors greeted the Singapore carrier's US$825 million planned acquisition of the American company by boosting NOL's share price to an eight-month high of Singapore $1.39 (US$0.97) in active morning trade on Tuesday. The share price eased to close at S$1.26, up five percent on the day.
NOL officials said the takeover of APL will make the firm a major global carrier, capturing about 10 percent of the trans-Pacific trade route.
The merger would catapult NOL into the big league, to be one of the top five carriers in the world with turnover reaching S$6 billion.
The planned acquisition, which is subject to approvals from U.S. regulators and APL shareholders, was announced at the weekend.

Under the takeover, NOL would buy all 24.6 million outstanding APL shares at US$33.50 each, making APL a wholly-owned subsidiary. Trading of NOL shares resumed on Tuesday after being suspended on Friday pending the announcement.

Shipping analysts applauded the NOL move, viewing it in a similar light to the merger announced between Holland's Nedlloyd Group and Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company (P&O) last September.

"NOL has said the merger will result in cost savings of US$130 million and that is very positive. But it is a question of how soon they can realise this," said Wong Leong Mein, investment analyst with ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett Securities.
Analysts said the near term outlook for shipping companies remains weak, with freight rates still under pressure due to overcapacity in the industry.
"Freight rates have been falling and will continue to fall. Shipping companies have to merge in order to survive," said Puja Chopra, investment analyst with JM Sassoon.
"The merger would put NOL in a much better position to compete globally," said Wong.
Analysts said NOL's shipping operations were barely profitable in 1996 and the company's bottom line was saved by ship sales.
The group's 1996 net profit halved to S$20.7 million from the previous year. Turnover rose three percent to S$1.93 billion.

Analysts said they expect NOL's earnings to be boosted this year by the APL acquisition. APL made a net profit of US$69.5 million in 1996 and analysts expect the U.S. firm to make just slightly less money in 1997 as last year's earnings included some exceptional items.
"APL is very profitable and the money it makes should cover interest costs for the acquisition," said one analyst with a Singapore firm.
NOL's borrowings currently stand at about S$2 billion and gearing for the group is expected to rise to about 3.6 times from about two times currently.
An analyst with a European firm said NOL should have no problems financing the acquisition as the group's cash flow is strong.
Analysts said other benefits NOL stands to reap from the takeover, would be instant recognition and access to the United States market.
